what_its_for: Nebivolol is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering your blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. Your doctor may also prescribe it for heart failure or other heart conditions.
how_to_take: Take nebivolol by mouth, with or without food, once a day. Swallow the tablet whole. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first — stopping too quickly can cause serious heart problems.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 5 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose over time, up to 40 mg per day, depending on how your body responds. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store nebivolol at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Store in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol while taking nebivolol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much. Do not take over-the-counter cold, flu, or allergy medicines without checking with your pharmacist first, since some of these can raise your blood pressure or interfere with this medicine. Avoid suddenly stopping this medication without your doctor's guidance.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: a very slow heartbeat (fewer than 60 beats per minute), dizziness or fainting, shortness of breath or swelling in your legs or ankles, sudden weight gain, chest pain, or signs of low blood sugar if you are diabetic (nebivolol can mask some symptoms). Seek emergency help immediately if you have signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Nebivolol starts working within a few hours of your first dose, but it may take 1 to 2 weeks before you notice the full benefit on your blood pressure. Keep taking it every day even if you feel fine, because high blood pressure often has no symptoms. Regular check-ups and blood pressure monitoring are important.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with caution; you may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness or slow heart rate. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Pregnancy: Do not use nebivolol during pregnancy unless your doctor says it is absolutely necessary — it may harm the unborn baby. Breastfeeding: It is not known if nebivolol passes into breast milk; talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in patients under 18 years old. Diabetics: Be aware that nebivolol may hide some signs of low blood sugar; monitor your blood sugar levels closely.
